result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers use an inventory, group the pages, and sample the large groups. Both invent no figures about the site and both run over the word limit. B wins narrowly: its rule for what gets read closely versus spot-checked is clearer, and its director report includes ranked recommendations with effort estimates. A's report says less about what each fix would take, though A handles ownership and per-group rules well. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give a solid, realistic six-week plan built on an inventory, group sorting and sampling. B ties its sampling more clearly to a decision rule for each group and gives owners and review triggers a firmer place. It also tells the user to take every count from their own inventory, while A brings in loose figures like 'top ~50', 'about 10%' and the expectation that most pages fall into a few groups. A's report section is a little stronger on effort estimates, but both answers run past the 700-word limit.
